title: Cross-model quantization safety and perf harness with p95/regression alerting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient, multi-workload benchmarking harness that exercises FP16, INT8, and INT4 quantization profiles across model families and detects regressions in latency (p95), throughput (tokens/sec), and output quality. The goal is to provide automated quality/performance trade-off matrices and timely alerts when quantized builds degrade user-facing metrics beyond agreed thresholds. This ticket covers harness design, runner implementation, result aggregation, and an initial alerting prototype integrated with Grafana/Slack.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 3 quant profiles (FP16, INT8, INT4) on the same model artifact with identical prompts and workloads
Aggregated metrics include tokens/sec, p95 latency, median latency, and quality scores for each profile
Automated regression detection flags a profile when quality drops >3% absolute or p95 increases >20% versus baseline
Alerts created in Grafana trigger a Slack channel with links to the failing run and summary report
Results exported as CSV/JSON and stored in S3 for secondary analysis
proposed_run_plan: Phase 1: Design doc and API for harness components (orchestrator, runner, aggregator, validator). Link: Confluence design above
Phase 2: Implement runner adapters for hosted and dedicated endpoints with configurable batching and warmup steps
Phase 3: Quality evaluator: embedding-similarity + token-level metrics + small human-review sampling script
Phase 4: Aggregation + statistical test (Mann-Whitney U for latency distributions, bootstrap for quality diffs) and control-chart based regression detector
Phase 5: Integrate Grafana alerting and Slack noisy/quiet modes; run smoke sweep across 3 representative models and 4 workloads
Phase 6: Document runbook and onboarding checklist for future quant rollouts
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Scope is intentionally broad to cover harness + alerting. Suggest we limit first run to 3 models: one small (7B), one medium (13B), one large (34B) to exercise kernel selection differences.

2025-02-14 Liam Chen: Implemented runner prototype that supports per-request batching and KV cache warmup. Observed large variance in INT4 runs for 34B on shared hardware; recommend adding multi-seed runs and longer warmup to reduce noise.

2025-02-15 Sofia Martinez (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; suggest lowering quality threshold for INT4 to account for expected drop but flag for manual review when quality drop >5% absolute. Also request export hooks for Console cost analysis.
2025-02-17 Priya Rao (Eng reviewer): Code review feedback on runner: separate retry/backoff for transient errors, add per-run metadata tags (model_version, quant_profile, batch_size, seq_len_dist).

2025-02-18 Liam Chen: Added aggregation pipeline that computes tokens/sec by dividing total_generated_tokens by effective_compute_time (minus warmup). Also added p95 and p99 histograms. Pushing branch for review: PR #182.

2025-02-19 Reliability note: During a load sweep, dedicated pool preemption caused intermittent tail latency spikes. Added a pre-check to ensure pool isolation or fall back to hosted variant for consistent measurement.

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Merged initial harness components; next action is to run a full 48-hour stability sweep and produce the first trade-off matrix. Liam to drive runs; Sofia to coordinate human review sampling for INT4 runs.
results_summary: initial-run: FP16 baseline established for three models. INT8 shows ~12-18% throughput improvement and negligible quality regression (<1.5% on embedding-similarity). INT4 yields 25-40% throughput gains for small/medium models but exhibits quality variance on large models; p95 increased by ~10% on 34B in shared env. Full stability sweep scheduled.
notes: Key trade-offs: INT8 gives strong cost/latency wins with low quality risk for most workloads. INT4 is promising for cost-sensitive batch workloads but requires workload-specific calibration and selective rollout (canary by traffic slice). We should add per-route fallback policies in Console tied to harness-derived thresholds.
next_steps: Run 48h stability sweep across targeted models and workloads (generation, chat, embedding reranking)
Tune INT4 calibration and repeat runs with isolated dedicated pools to remove preemption noise
Wire regression detector to Skaffold/Grafana panels and create playbook for triage
Prepare short PRD for conservative rollout policy (canary by percentage + auto-fallback) and handoff to Console team
